statement: A finite set $S$ of distinct positive reals is \textit{radiant} if for any two distinct $a, b \in S$, $a^2 + b^2 \in S$. (a) Does there exist a radiant set of size $\geq 4$? (b) Determine all radiant sets of size 2 or 3.

A $2n \times 2n$ grid is \textit{balanced} if each cell contains $-1$, $0$, or $1$ and the absolute sum of all entries is at most $4n$. Find the smallest $k \geq 1$ such that any balanced grid contains an $n \times n$ square whose absolute entry sum is $\leq k$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ have circumcircle $\omega$ with center $O$. Let $P \in BC$; let $Q$ be the second intersection of the circumcircles of $\triangle AOB$ and $\triangle APC$. Prove that line $PQ$ and the tangent to $\omega$ at $A$ meet on the circumcircle of $\triangle AOB$.

Charlotte writes $1, 2, \ldots, 2025$ on a board and may apply GCD or LCM operations (pick two numbers, erase them, write their gcd or lcm). A number $N$ is \textit{winning} if some sequence of operations leaves only $N$. Find all winning numbers in $\{1,\ldots,2025\}$ and for each determine the minimum number of GCD operations needed.

Let $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ be a sequence of positive integers such that for all $k < \ell$ and all distinct $m_1,\ldots,m_k$ and distinct $n_1,\ldots,n_\ell$, $a_{m_1}+\cdots+a_{m_k} \leq a_{n_1}+\cdots+a_{n_\ell}$. Prove there exist integers $N$ and $b$ such that $a_n = b$ for all $n \geq N$.
Same as Junior P2: find the smallest $k$ such that any balanced $2n \times 2n$ grid contains an $n \times n$ square with absolute entry sum $\leq k$.

Let $\omega$ be a circle with center $O$, and $B, C$ fixed points on $\omega$. Let $A$ vary on $\omega$. Let $X = OB \cap AC$ ($X \neq O$); $\gamma$ = circumcircle of $\triangle AOX$; $Y$ = second intersection of $\gamma$ with $\omega$; tangent to $\gamma$ at $Y$ meets $\omega$ at $I$; $J$ = second intersection of $OI$ with $\omega$; perpendicular bisector of $OY$ meets $YI$ at $T$; $AJ$ meets $\gamma$ at $P$; $Z$ = second intersection of circumcircle of $\triangle PYT$ with $\omega$. Prove $Y$ and $Z$ are fixed as $A$ varies.

Find all sequences of positive integers $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ satisfying: (i) there exists $M > 0$ with $0 < a_n \leq M$ for all $n$; (ii) for any prime $p$ and any $n \geq 1$, $p \mid a_n a_{n+1} \cdots a_{n+p-1} - a_{n+p}$.
